answer: Sybil resistance is enforced with a sealed walnut commitment: each applicant binds a unique hardware or wallet fingerprint and posts a time-locked bond before it can trade. The new identity may then earn protocol nectar only by completing paid tasks inside a supervised reef marketplace, where payouts vest on a delay and withdrawals need a sliding window of distinct counterparties. Sockpuppet factories therefore cannot cash out until each alias has transacted with many independent agents, so the cost of a swarm scales with real economic activity rather than with free account creation.
